GitHub Copilot on GitHub.com can answer questions about your repositories, plan and make changes, review pull requests, and automate repository tasks.
Automations run repository tasks on a schedule or in response to events, rather than requiring a new prompt each time.

Tried the beta of GitHub's iOS app and didn't find a single bug. Really enjoyed using it to casually browse code on the phone and would highly recommend it to programmers who look at repos on mobile. Lost beta access after not using it for about 14 days.

Couldn't find the app by searching the Apple App Store; only the link in the blog post worked. Another user: App Store search is so bad it's 'basically impossible to find this by searching for "GitHub"' among the sea of other GitHub apps.
Following a link in a readme to another file within the GitHub repo always results in 'something went wrong' (iOS).

Android beta has a lot of paper cuts: diff lines wrap, and the large code font makes wrapping frequent, so code review is harder. Per-commit review is even harder. No main activity feed. Links to a specific issue comment land at the top of the issue. Still an improvement over mobile web, where the PR approve button was hard to hit.

Biggest gripe on Android: clicking a GitHub link to a new repo asks whether to open it in Chrome or GitHub, for every single repo. The URL intent handler seems to treat each repo as a different intent.
It seemed to allow sign-in without 2FA despite org enforcement. After signing out of both the browser and the app, it did prompt for 2FA; it had been reusing the browser token.
Doesn't really seem to be a git client, more the social fluff. Working Copy is still the best git client for iOS.
Really great, has push notifications. But there is no push notification for when you're assigned to review a PR, which is really annoying.
Only wish is multiple account support; has both a personal and a work account.
Nice, at least at first glance, on the iPad.
Uses FastHub / FastHub-Libre and doesn't intend to switch. Finds it ironic if Microsoft's GitHub app isn't open source; others also couldn't find the app's source code.
Has used Octodroid for years and says it already does everything the official app does. Won't bother trying the official GitHub app.

Got an invitation to test the iOS GitHub app but couldn't use it because the account was flagged as spam, apparently after reporting spammers in a public Gist, despite a long record of open-source contributions.
